newsitem.title: USA: Alhambra, Calif, to file $50 mln suit over traffic.
newsitem.headline: Alhambra, Calif, to file $50 mln suit over traffic.

text.p: Alhambra, Calif., said on Monday it planned to file a $50 million suit against federal transportation officials over increased traffic congestion.

In a statement, the city said the suit would allege that federal transportation officials discriminated against the city's minority residents by failing to permit the completion of a 6.2-mile gap in Interstate 710.
The city said the gap has put 100,000 vehicles daily on Alhambra streets, creating 4.8 tons of carbon monoxide each day. The city said its ethnic minorities are hardest hit.
The suit will name as defendants U.S. Secretary of Transportation Federico Pena and Director of the Federal Highway Administration Rodney Slater, the city said.
In addition, the city said it would file suit to block southern California's Alameda Corridor project, also citing the environmental impact on the community.
The city said it would provide additional details about the suits at a press briefing Tuesday at Alhambra City Hall.
